card.name: Opioid drug appositive "a" after name
card.fires_on: The word "a" right after a comma following an opioid drug name, where a description like "a Schedule II controlled substance" or "a mixed agonist/antagonist opioid" comes next. Also small linking words just before a drug name in opioid warnings.

modes.label: Appositive after drug name
modes.description: The word "a" after "drugname," introducing a class or schedule description of an opioid.
modes.example: Pentazocine and Naloxone Tablets contain pentazocine,<< a>> Schedule IV controlled substance.

modes.label: Linking word before a drug
modes.description: Small words such as "and", "use" or "other" just before a named drug or medication in opioid warnings.
modes.example: Avoid the use of belladonna<< and>> opium suppositories in patients with circ

modes.label: Inside a drug name
modes.description: The middle of a drug ingredient name, partway through the word.
modes.example: items exposed to capsa<<ic>>in, then touching the eyes and muc

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words meaning drug, medicine or agent, and away from sedation and pain words.
card.plain: It fires at the spot where the text is about to describe an opioid drug as a kind of medicine or controlled substance.
